title: Isandro and the Yearbook
premise: Emrys Underhill has survived two years at Ashgrove Academy by being forgettable—until his best friend Isandro Vane, keeper of the school's century-old yearbook tradition, vanishes the night before the Founders' Game, leaving only a ring of keys and a yearbook page torn from 1974. Following the keys through the academy's hidden rooms, Emrys uncovers that the 'tradition' is a cover for a decades-old pact between the school's founding families: each generation, one scholarship student is erased from the record to protect their legacy. Isandro discovered he was this year's chosen sacrifice and staged his own disappearance to force someone to finally look. In the climactic last game of the season, Emrys exposes the pact publicly by reading the erased names aloud at halftime, choosing love for Isandro over the safety of invisibility; the boys reunite as the town reckons with what its beloved tradition truly cost.
about_author: Freya Nystrom is a former boarding school archivist who spent years cataloguing other people's secrets before writing her own. She lives in a coastal town where every autumn still smells faintly of bonfires and unfinished business.

chapters.title: The Boy Who Was Fine
chapters.summary: Emrys's POV. Establishes his careful invisibility at Ashgrove: perfect grades, no enemies, no presence. Isandro drags him into helping archive the yearbooks, teasing him about being 'a ghost who types.' Emotional beat: warmth disguised as routine, and the first hint that Isandro is watching Emrys more closely than anyone should.

chapters.title: Keys on the Windowsill
chapters.summary: Emrys's POV. The morning after the Founders' Bonfire, Isandro is gone. No texts, no note—just seven old keys labeled in his handwriting and a torn yearbook page from 1974 showing a student's face scratched out. Emotional beat: cold dread beneath Emrys's practiced calm; the police call it a runaway.

chapters.title: Everyone Says Runaway
chapters.summary: Emrys's POV alternating with brief Isandro flashbacks. The school closes ranks; Headmaster Crane calls Isandro 'troubled,' and even Isandro's wealthy family seems oddly unbothered. Emotional beat: isolation deepening—the only person who saw Emrys is now the person no one will discuss.

chapters.title: The First Key Opens Nothing
chapters.summary: Emrys's POV. Key one fits the old chapel crypt, which contains nothing but dust—until Emrys notices fresh scratches in the lock. Someone else has been here recently. Emotional beat: fear sharpening into purpose; Emrys realizes he's not the only one searching.

chapters.title: Hall of Names
chapters.summary: Emrys's POV. Key two opens a corridor of founder portraits, each paired with a yearbook. Comparing editions, Emrys finds it: every twenty-five years, one scholarship student's photo is missing or defaced. Emotional beat: vertigo—the pattern is deliberate, institutional, old.

chapters.title: The Girl Who Wasn't There
chapters.summary: Emrys's POV with a 1974 flashback chapter from missing student Wren Calloway's perspective. Wren was 'transferred' mid-year; her records end in a single line. Emotional beat: grief across time—Emrys understands he's reading a disappearance that worked perfectly.

chapters.title: Duty Wears a Blazer
chapters.summary: Alternating POV: Margot Ashgrove, heir to the founding family and Emrys's reluctant study partner, is pressured by her grandmother to keep the Game preparations flawless. Emotional beat: Margot's guilt introduced—she knows more than she says, and duty is starting to feel like a cage.

chapters.title: Key Three, Locked From Inside
chapters.summary: Emrys's POV. A sub-basement room beneath the gym holds the 'Ledger of Continuity'—the pact itself, signed by generations of founders. The door locks behind him; he escapes through a coal chute as footsteps approach. Emotional beat: terror confirming the stakes—this secret defends itself.

chapters.title: Margot Knows Something
chapters.summary: Dual POV. Emrys confronts Margot; she admits the families maintain 'an arrangement' but claims she doesn't know details. Her grandmother burns a box of archives that night. Emotional beat: uneasy alliance—two people using each other while wanting to trust each other.

chapters.title: What Isandro Left Me
chapters.summary: Emrys's POV. Decoding Isandro's key labels as dates, Emrys maps them to the erased students' enrollment years—and realizes the final key is dated this year. His name isn't on it. Isandro's is. Emotional beat: heartbreak and fury—Isandro knew, and chose to vanish rather than be quietly deleted.

chapters.title: The Tradition Everyone Loves
chapters.summary: Town-wide POV mosaic. The Founders' Game approaches; shopkeepers hang banners; alumni return. Interwoven: an elderly alumna privately tells Emrys she remembers Wren Calloway's face. Emotional beat: the horror of complicity—a whole town built on a beautiful lie.

chapters.title: Crane's Offer
chapters.summary: Emrys's POV. Headmaster Crane offers Emrys a full ride, any university, if he stops asking questions and returns the keys. He mentions Emrys's mother's debts. Emotional beat: temptation made flesh—invisibility was never free, just subsidized.

chapters.title: Margot Breaks
chapters.summary: Margot's POV. Her grandmother reveals Margot's own role: as the founder's heir, she must formally 'approve' this year's continuity at the Game. Margot finds Isandro's hidden letter in her late father's papers—he'd begged her family for help weeks ago. Emotional beat: shattering loyalty; she chooses Emrys over blood.

chapters.title: Where the Keys Don't Go
chapters.summary: Emrys and Margot's POV. Realizing the seventh key fits nothing on campus, they trace it to the decommissioned lighthouse keeper's cottage the founders still own. Emotional beat: hope with teeth—they're close, and so is whoever locked Emrys in the basement.

chapters.title: The Cottage at Low Tide
chapters.summary: Emrys's POV. In the cottage: Isandro's journal, food wrappers, a plan scrawled on the wall—he's been hiding, documenting everything, waiting to see if anyone would come. A note: 'If you're reading this, you looked. That's all I ever wanted.' Emotional beat: relief curdling into urgency—Isandro plans to walk into the Game and expose everything alone, badly.

chapters.title: Nineteen Seventy-Four, Continued
chapters.summary: Wren's flashback POV concludes: she didn't transfer—she was escorted out at dawn, sworn to silence, her life rerouted. Present-day: Emrys finds Wren alive, three towns over, running a bookshop. Emotional beat: survival without justice—proof the erased don't die, but they do disappear.

chapters.title: The Night Before the Game
chapters.summary: Triple POV: Emrys, Margot, Isandro. Emrys convinces Wren to come; Margot prepares to refuse the rite publicly; Isandro leaves the cottage knowing it may be a trap. Emotional beat: converging courage—each chooses exposure over safety, separately, before dawn.

chapters.title: Founders' Game, First Half
chapters.summary: Ensemble POV. The stadium roars; Crane watches Emrys; Margot's grandmother grips the rite ledger; Isandro slips into the crowd hooded. Emotional beat: unbearable suspense—everything ordinary, which is exactly how the erasure always happened.

chapters.title: Halftime
chapters.summary: Emrys's POV. At the microphone during the tradition ceremony, instead of the scripted tribute, Emrys reads the names: Wren Calloway, and every erased student since 1911. Margot refuses the rite aloud. Wren walks onto the field. Emotional beat: cathartic rupture—the invisible made unbearably visible.

chapters.title: The Last Key
chapters.summary: Climax, Emrys and Isandro POV. Chaos erupts; Crane tries to cut the sound; Isandro reveals himself and hands Emrys the seventh key—it opens the stadium's cornerstone time capsule holding the original pact, signed proof, broadcast on the jumbotron. Emotional beat: triumph and terror entwined; the truth is public and irreversible.

chapters.title: After the Whistle
chapters.summary: Resolution, ensemble POV. Investigations begin; Crane resigns; the founding families settle with the erased students' descendants. Isandro returns to school—not as a ghost, but as himself. Emotional beat: tender aftermath; justice arrived outside any courtroom, carried by witnesses.

chapters.title: Emrys Underhill, Recorded
chapters.summary: Epilogue, Emrys's POV. Spring: the new yearbook goes to print. Isandro photographs Emrys for his portrait—the first time anyone's insisted he be seen. Final line mirrors the opening: he's fine. Actually fine. Emotional beat: quiet joy—identity chosen, not assigned; love that outlasted duty.
